items.title: Exception silently swallowed
items.why: An empty except/catch hides failures, including failed auth or payment calls, and makes incidents very hard to debug.

items.title: Retired or deprecated model hardcoded
items.why: The provider has retired (or announced the retirement of) this model id, so requests fail or will fail without warning.

items.title: LLM call without an output token limit
items.why: Without max tokens a single request (or a prompt-injected loop) can generate very long, expensive responses.

items.title: Database query inside a loop (N+1)
items.why: One query per item turns a page with 100 rows into 101 round trips: slow pages, timeouts and database load that grows with your data.

items.title: Cross-site scripting through a raw HTML sink
items.why: Inserting unsanitized data as HTML (innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, v-html, {@html}, |safe) lets an attacker run JavaScript in other users' browsers and steal their sessions.

items.title: Admin or database port open to the internet
items.why: A security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH, RDP or a database port gets scanned and brute-forced within minutes of going up.

items.title: Auth token stored in localStorage
items.why: Any XSS bug can read localStorage and steal the token, so one script injection becomes account takeover.

items.title: Third-party GitHub Action not pinned to a commit
items.why: A tag like `@v3` can be moved by whoever controls the action's repository; if it is compromised, your workflow runs their code with your secrets and token (as in the tj-actions/changed-files attack).

items.title: SQL injection
items.why: Building SQL with string formatting lets an attacker change the query: read other users' data, bypass login or drop tables.

items.title: Secret written to logs
items.why: Logs are copied to hosting dashboards, log services and screenshots. Printing a key leaks it there.

items.title: Environment variable missing from the example env file
items.why: The code reads a variable that .env.example does not document, so the next deploy or teammate setup crashes or silently runs with a missing setting.

items.title: Form field without a label
items.why: Without a label, screen readers announce only "edit text", and placeholder text disappears as soon as the user types.

items.title: Dangerous agent or framework option enabled
items.why: This option gives the model arbitrary code, shell or network execution (for example allow_dangerous_code=True or a Python REPL tool).

items.title: State-changing endpoint without authentication
items.why: This endpoint creates, changes or deletes data but no authentication check was found, so anyone on the internet can call it directly, whatever the UI shows.

items.title: Foreign key without an index
items.why: Postgres does not index foreign key columns. Every delete or key update in the referenced table, and every join on the key, scans the referencing table; with ON DELETE CASCADE it also locks it.

items.title: Database query inside a loop (N+1)
items.why: One query per item turns a page with 100 rows into 101 round trips: slow pages, timeouts and database load that grows with your data.

items.title: Container runs as root
items.why: If the app is compromised the attacker is root inside the container, which makes escaping and tampering easier.

items.title: Insecure CORS policy
items.why: Allowing any or a reflected origin together with credentials lets any website call your API as the logged-in user. (An open origin without credentials is not reported: no cookies are sent.)

items.title: Timestamp without time zone
items.why: Naive datetimes and `timestamp without time zone` columns silently mix local and UTC times, which breaks expiry checks, schedules and reports across regions and daylight saving.

items.title: Possible insecure direct object reference (IDOR)
items.why: The handler changes a record by the id in the URL but never compares it with the current user, so any logged-in user can change anyone's data by changing the id.

items.title: Webhook without signature verification
items.why: Without verifying the provider's signature anyone can post fake events, for example marking an order as paid.

items.title: No automated tests
items.why: AI-generated code often looks right and is subtly wrong. Without tests nobody notices until users do, and every future AI edit can silently break existing behaviour.

items.title: No health-check endpoint
items.why: Load balancers, containers and uptime monitors need a cheap endpoint to tell a dead instance from a live one.

items.title: Any Host header accepted
items.why: ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] enables host header attacks such as poisoned password-reset links.

items.title: Redis key without an expiry
items.why: Keys written without a TTL stay until something deletes them; caches, sessions and rate-limit counters then grow until Redis runs out of memory or starts evicting keys you need.
